summary: Defined the one-day local FastAPI architecture, exact five-rule semantics, stable evidence scheme, bounded one-call Gemini trust boundary, graceful failure contract, component impacts, and independent verification expectations without adding database, frontend, infrastructure, or production scope.
decisions: DEMO-001 is one local Python/FastAPI/Pydantic backend plus FastAPI /docs. Database, persistence, separate frontend, deployment, container, cloud resource, identity, retrieval, agent framework, and production observability components remain disabled and require no workers for this task.

The runtime path is a thin POST /api/v1/analyze-demo route over an analysis service, fixed allowlisted read-only loader, minimal supported-subset extractor/evidence index, pure rule engine, injected Gemini summarizer adapter, and response assembler. The injected summarizer boundary lets tests use fakes without live credentials.

Only dataset/patient_bbuser29999.json, dataset/coverage_bundle_bbuser29999.json, and dataset/eob_bundle_bbuser29999.json are application inputs. The loader resolves fixed project-owned locations, reads without writes, rejects files above 1 MiB, and applies the documented Bundle/item/adjudication/coding/string limits. Parsed monetary values are finite Decimals and currencies are never converted or inferred.

Minimal validation confirms UTF-8 JSON objects, the standalone Patient and homogeneous searchset Coverage/EOB Bundle shapes, required supported fields, bounded collections, full ISO dates used by rules, finite amounts, and non-empty references/identities. It is deliberately not base FHIR, profile, CARIN, NCPDP, or terminology conformance validation.

Supported resource identities are indexed one-to-many by exact resourceType/id. Duplicate identities are preserved so REF-001 can signal ambiguous resolution rather than a parser overwriting evidence; references are local relative expected-type strings only and are never dereferenced.

Fact evidence IDs are application-generated from fixed source aliases and RFC 6901 JSON pointers. Signal evidence IDs use stable rule IDs and zero-padded ordinals after rule-owned canonical sorting. Untrusted identifiers, codes, displays, provider text, and model text cannot mint evidence IDs.

REF-001 checks Coverage beneficiary, EOB patient, and every EOB insurance Coverage reference for missing, malformed, wrong-type, unresolved, or multiply resolved local references. DATE-001 compares item.servicedDate inclusively only against present bounds of uniquely resolved referenced Coverages and records absent dates/bounds as missing evidence without substituting billablePeriod.

REPEAT-001 defines an exact duplicate by equal patient reference, sorted Coverage references, servicedDate, product/service system+code, and selected benefit/paidbypatient/drugcost value+currency tuples across distinct source paths. It separately signals exact system+code repetition at count two or more across the whole supplied EOB sample; it performs no near-match or code/display interpretation.

AMOUNT-001 selects benefit from the exact base adjudication system and paidbypatient/drugcost from the exact observed C4BB adjudication system. It evaluates only one finite same-currency value for each and signals when abs(drugcost - (benefit + paidbypatient)) exceeds Decimal 0.01; missing/duplicate/currency-conflicting components are missing evidence rather than zero and every mismatch carries an unmodeled-components limitation.

OUTLIER-001 groups usable drugcost values by exact currency, requires at least four observations, uses Tukey hinges, and signals values strictly above Q3 + 1.5*IQR. The unchanged ten-value USD sample produces Q1=0, Q3=20, threshold=50, and one 100 USD signal; this is sample-relative only.

Every rule exposes execution status, zero or more canonically ordered signals, exact inputs/formula/threshold, evidence, missing evidence, and limitations. Priority labels are informational/review-only and cannot be represented as fraud, healthcare risk, clinical, coding, payment, coverage, or medical-necessity judgments.

The Gemini adapter uses the Google Gen AI SDK configured for Vertex AI, makes zero calls when configuration is absent and otherwise at most one call, exposes no tools/loops/side effects, and sends only minimized structured synthetic facts, deterministic signals, supplied evidence IDs, and limitations. It uses a 30-second total timeout, 2,048 output-token ceiling, 128 KiB prompt ceiling, and 64 KiB structured-content ceiling.

Gemini output is untrusted until Pydantic bounds and the evidence allowlist pass. It is limited to a 2,000-character summary, five candidate findings, ten missing-evidence statements, and ten limitations; each finding has bounded text and one to ten unique supplied citations. Unknown/missing citations or any bound/schema failure reject the entire Gemini portion without a repair call.

The contract uses HTTP 200 whenever deterministic analysis succeeds, including typed Gemini statuses success, configuration_error, timeout, provider_error, invalid_output, and invalid_evidence. Only success may contain candidate findings. Source/shape/limit failure makes no model call and returns a sanitized HTTP 500 code without raw exception or provider text.

contracts/openapi.yaml must change from its empty placeholder before CONTRACT_READY. It must define the bodyless endpoint, separated fact/evidence/rule/Gemini/limitation/metadata schemas, all model statuses, deterministic error codes, response bounds, and citation requirements; implementation workers must consume rather than edit the approved contract.

Independent testing is required. Unit and integration evidence must cover every rule's signal/no-signal/missing-evidence paths, stable IDs, bounds and malformed shapes, fake model success/configuration/timeout/provider/parsing/schema/citation failures, zero/one-call enforcement, contract alignment, no live credentials, and source hashes before/after.

No new ADR is needed because ADR-0001 through ADR-0004 already authorize and constrain human authority, synthetic-only input, the simplified local platform, and direct bounded Vertex AI Gemini use. This task refines those accepted decisions rather than introducing a project-wide platform choice.

risks.description: Deterministic signals or fluent Gemini explanations could be presented as fraud, coverage, payment, coding, clinical, medical-necessity, CARIN-conformance, or production-validity conclusions.
risks.mitigation: Use the exact narrow rule wording, informational/review-only labels, candidate-only model section, mandatory global limitations, and ADR-0001 human-authority boundary in contract, implementation, README, tests, security review, and final review.

risks.description: Untrusted FHIR strings or model output could cause prompt injection, citation fabrication, secret leakage, active rendering, or unintended external behavior.
risks.mitigation: Serialize only minimized bounded data, separate instructions from data, expose no tools or URL/file access, keep secrets/configuration out of payloads and logs, validate Pydantic output and every citation, render JSON only, and reject the complete model portion on failure.

risks.description: A provider/configuration/timeout/output failure could erase deterministic evidence or trigger multiple costly/uncontrolled calls.
risks.mitigation: Assemble deterministic results before the adapter, enforce zero or one invocation, prohibit repair/fallback calls, map all model failures to typed sanitized HTTP 200 partial states, and independently test call counts and retained deterministic sections.

risks.description: Floating-point parsing, duplicate adjudication categories, currency mismatch, or an ambiguous quartile method could make amount signals irreproducible or misleading.
risks.mitigation: Use finite Decimal parsing, require exactly one same-currency selected component, freeze tolerance at 0.01, define Tukey hinges and strict threshold comparison, expose formula metadata, and test boundary/even/odd/missing cases.

risks.description: Fixed local files could be mutated, replaced, oversized, or accidentally accessed through current-working-directory or arbitrary-path behavior.
risks.mitigation: Resolve only the three fixed project-owned locations, accept no request path/upload/URL, enforce byte and structure bounds before extraction, never open for write, and prove repository dataset hashes are unchanged before and after tests.

risks.description: The one-beneficiary, ten-EOB sample can make repetition and high-amount signals look generalizable when they are only demonstrations.
risks.mitigation: Record sample counts/formulas/evidence, state small-sample limitations in every response and README, use project-authored synthetic test variants only outside dataset/, and make no population, payer, healthcare-validity, or benchmark claim.

risks.description: Adding authentication, persistence, custom UI, deployment, terminology validation, retries, telemetry, or other production concerns would jeopardize the one-day milestone and change trust boundaries.
risks.mitigation: Keep all such components explicitly disabled, reject incidental scaffold as a dependency, run only the backend/contract/test workers selected by impacts, and require a later approved scope and architecture decision for expansion.

risks.description: Unauthenticated FastAPI /docs could be mistaken for an approved shared or deployed interface.
risks.mitigation: Bind conservatively for local development, document synthetic local use, add no deployment artifacts, and state that any networked/shared use requires a new authentication and security architecture.

notes_for_next_agent: Orchestrator/contract owner: replace only the DEMO-001 OpenAPI placeholder and validate it before CONTRACT_READY; use the exact endpoint/failure/citation boundaries above and do not import historical DATA-001 CARIN contracts.

Backend owner: work only in backend/**, tests/backend/**, README.md, .env.example, and backend-report.json; keep dataset/** read-only and do not edit contracts, task.json, database, or frontend paths.

Backend owner: keep model construction behind an injected adapter, create deterministic results before invocation, and make fake-client tests prove configuration-free, timeout, provider, invalid-output, invalid-evidence, and one-call behavior.
Do not start database, frontend, or infrastructure work: their impact flags are false and FastAPI /docs is the complete interface.

Tester: independently own tests/** additions and test-report.json, preserve backend-authored tests, verify exact rule math/statuses/IDs, exercise contract responses, and compare hashes of all three approved dataset files before and after.

Security and final review should focus on source allowlisting/immutability, prompt minimization, secret/error redaction, output/citation validation, bounded one-call enforcement, safe wording, and absence of production/CARIN/compliance/healthcare-validity claims.
